AMD FidelityFX SDK 1.1.4 (MIT): frame interpolation and optical flow, with changes that let one
pair of frames yield several generated frames, and the recipe that builds it for Linux
(ffx_fg/, GPL-3.0-or-later). Taken on 2026-11-13 from the authors' own modified
build of Lichii (an emulator made to run Nintendo Switch 2 games; the build is a local one) at its
commit 8618ffe51f, where these changes and the recipe were first written. The approach, building
AMD's FSR 3 frame interpolation from its sources on Linux and giving it a game's own depth and
motion vectors with a HUD-free picture, was found in a fork of the PS5 emulator KytyPS5
(https://github.com/chenxiao07/KytyPS5, pull requests #117 and #118 by Bios2000; GPL-2.0-only). It
served as a guide and none of its code was taken. Myrddin's frame generation from a game's motion
vectors is its authors' own implementation, not third-party work.

  ffx/include/   the SDK's headers, as the layer is built against
  ffx_src/       the SDK's sources and the build recipe (./build.sh -> build/ffx/ffx_fg/libffx_fg.a)
  lichii/        Vulkan test helpers and the compatibility header the layer is built with
                 (GPL-3.0-or-later)

Adwaita Sans (SIL Open Font License 1.1): the letters of the layer's panel are a rendering of it
(fg/hud_font.h, made by tools/make-hud-font.py from Fedora's adwaita-sans-fonts 50.0, font version 4.001).

  adwaita-sans/LICENSE   the font's copyright notices and the licence text, as its package carries them
